title: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord
body:
Read the chapter → [Leviticus 23](/bible/leviticus/23)

**[Leviticus 23:1-3](/bible/leviticus/23#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/leviticus/23#v1)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/leviticus/23#v2)</sup> Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of the Lord, which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/leviticus/23#v3)</sup> Six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest, an holy convocation; ye shall do no work therein: it is the sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings.

- These are the feasts of the Lord, holy convocations which He Himself proclaimed. The Most High gave us holy days; a holiday not listed in this Bible and not ordained of the Most High has nothing holy about it. By the knowledge of the Lord the days were distinguished: some He made high days, as the Passover, Tabernacles, the new moon, and the Sabbath, and the days He did not name are ordinary days.
- Six days shall work be done, but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest, an holy convocation. No matter where your dwelling is, Israel, North America, London, or Australia, the Sabbath is still the Sabbath: Friday sundown to Saturday sundown in whatever time zone you are in.
- Keeping the Sabbath holy is more than no working. Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day, so there is no cooking on the Sabbath; and if the people of the land bring ware or victuals on the sabbath day to sell, we would not buy it of them, so there is no buying and no selling.
- It is a holy convocation, which means a gathering. Keeping the Sabbath sitting at home with your gerbil or your hamster is not keeping the Sabbath; you have to come out of your comfort zone and congregate.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 33:7-9](/bible/sirach/33#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/sirach/33#v7)</sup> Why doth one day excel another, when as all the light of every day in the year is of the sun?
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/sirach/33#v8)</sup> By the knowledge of the Lord they were distinguished: and he altered seasons and feasts.
    >
    > <sup>[9](/bible/sirach/33#v9)</sup> Some of them hath he made high days, and hallowed them, and some of them hath he made ordinary days.

    One day excels another by the knowledge of the Lord: some days He made high days and hallowed them, and some He made ordinary.
  - **[Exodus 35:1-3](/bible/exodus/35#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/exodus/35#v1)</sup> And Moses gathered all the congregation of the children of Israel together, and said unto them, These are the words which the Lord hath commanded, that ye should do them.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/exodus/35#v2)</sup> Six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day there shall be to you an holy day, a sabbath of rest to the Lord: whosoever doeth work therein shall be put to death.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/exodus/35#v3)</sup> Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.

    On the holy sabbath day whosoever doeth work shall be put to death, and ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations; no cooking on the Sabbath.
  - **[Nehemiah 10:31](/bible/nehemiah/10#v31)**
    > <sup>[31](/bible/nehemiah/10#v31)</sup> And if the people of the land bring ware or any victuals on the sabbath day to sell, that we would not buy it of them on the sabbath, or on the holy day: and that we would leave the seventh year, and the exaction of every debt.

    If the people of the land bring ware or victuals on the sabbath day to sell, we would not buy it of them; no buying and no selling on the Sabbath.

**[Leviticus 23:4-8](/bible/leviticus/23#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/leviticus/23#v4)</sup> These are the feasts of the Lord, even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/leviticus/23#v5)</sup> In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/leviticus/23#v6)</sup> And on the fifteenth day of the same month is the feast of unleavened bread unto the Lord: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/leviticus/23#v7)</sup> In the first day ye shall have an holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/leviticus/23#v8)</sup> But ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord seven days: in the seventh day is an holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein.

- In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover. The fourteenth day at even means the fifteenth day, so the verse about the fifteenth day is saying the same thing: the first day of the Passover is also the first day of the feast of unleavened bread.
- On the first day and on the seventh day is an holy convocation: no buying, no selling, no servile work. But you can cook on the Passover, because there is no Passover without the Passover meal, the lamb, unleavened bread, and bitter herbs.
- On the last day of unleavened bread you may also cook, unless it falls on the seventh day Sabbath. The only time you can cook on the seventh day Sabbath is when the Passover falls on that day, because you cannot have the Passover without the lamb roast with fire; no other high holy day gives you a set meal, and no other feast overrides the Sabbath cooking prohibition.

  Precepts:
  - **[Luke 22:1](/bible/luke/22#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/luke/22#v1)</sup> Now the feast of unleavened bread drew nigh, which is called the Passover.

    The feast of unleavened bread is called the Passover; the two feasts run together as one.
  - **[1 Esdras 1:17-19](/bible/1-esdras/1#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/1-esdras/1#v17)</sup> Thus were the things that belonged to the sacrifices of the Lord accomplished in that day, that they might hold the passover,
    >
    > <sup>[18](/bible/1-esdras/1#v18)</sup> And offer sacrifices upon the altar of the Lord, according to the commandment of king Josias.
    >
    > <sup>[19](/bible/1-esdras/1#v19)</sup> So the children of Israel which were present held the passover at that time, and the feast of sweet bread seven days.

    In the days of Josias the feast of unleavened bread is called the feast of sweet bread, kept seven days with the passover.

**[Leviticus 23:9-14](/bible/leviticus/23#v9)**

> <sup>[9](/bible/leviticus/23#v9)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/leviticus/23#v10)</sup> Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, When ye be come into the land which I give unto you, and shall reap the harvest thereof, then ye shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest unto the priest:
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/leviticus/23#v11)</sup> And he shall wave the sheaf before the Lord, to be accepted for you: on the morrow after the sabbath the priest shall wave it.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/leviticus/23#v12)</sup> And ye shall offer that day when ye wave the sheaf an he lamb without blemish of the first year for a burnt offering unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/leviticus/23#v13)</sup> And the meat offering thereof shall be two tenth deals of fine flour mingled with oil, an offering made by fire unto the Lord for a sweet savour: and the drink offering thereof shall be of wine, the fourth part of an hin.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/leviticus/23#v14)</sup> And ye shall eat neither bread, nor parched corn, nor green ears, until the selfsame day that ye have brought an offering unto your God: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations in all your dwellings.

- When ye be come into the land, ye shall bring a sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest unto the priest, and he shall wave the sheaf before the Lord on the morrow after the sabbath, with an he lamb without blemish for a burnt offering.
- This wave sheaf day is what the New Testament calls the preparation: after the Passover was kept, the day following was the preparation, which prepared for this feast of the waving of the sheaf.
- Ye shall eat neither bread nor parched corn nor green ears until the selfsame day that ye have brought an offering unto your God; it is a statute for ever throughout your generations.

**[Leviticus 23:15-21](/bible/leviticus/23#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/leviticus/23#v15)</sup> And ye shall count unto you from the morrow after the sabbath, from the day that ye brought the sheaf of the wave offering; seven sabbaths shall be complete:
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/leviticus/23#v16)</sup> Even unto the morrow after the seventh sabbath shall ye number fifty days; and ye shall offer a new meat offering unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/leviticus/23#v17)</sup> Ye shall bring out of your habitations two wave loaves of two tenth deals: they shall be of fine flour; they shall be baken with leaven; they are the firstfruits unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/leviticus/23#v18)</sup> And ye shall offer with the bread seven lambs without blemish of the first year, and one young bullock, and two rams: they shall be for a burnt offering unto the Lord, with their meat offering, and their drink offerings, even an offering made by fire, of sweet savour unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/leviticus/23#v19)</sup> Then ye shall sacrifice one kid of the goats for a sin offering, and two lambs of the first year for a sacrifice of peace offerings.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/leviticus/23#v20)</sup> And the priest shall wave them with the bread of the firstfruits for a wave offering before the Lord, with the two lambs: they shall be holy to the Lord for the priest.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/leviticus/23#v21)</sup> And ye shall proclaim on the selfsame day, that it may be an holy convocation unto you: ye shall do no servile work therein: it shall be a statute for ever in all your dwellings throughout your generations.

- From the morrow after the sabbath, from the day the sheaf of the wave offering was brought, count seven sabbaths complete, seven times seven which is forty and nine, and the morrow after the seventh sabbath is the fiftieth day. That is why the feast is called Pentecost, from fifty, as a pentagon has five sides; it is also called the feast of weeks, because of the seven weeks that are counted.
- With the two wave loaves came burnt offerings, a sin offering, and peace offerings, meat offerings and drink offerings. That is what Colossians is talking about when it says let no man judge you in meat or in drink or in respect of an holyday: those who did not believe in Christ condemned the followers of Christ as wicked for not sacrificing on the holy days. We still keep the holy days, but we do not offer the offerings, because the body of Christ has been given.
- The meat offerings and drink offerings and carnal ordinances were a figure for the time then present, imposed until the time of reformation; they could not make him that did the service perfect as pertaining to the conscience. But Christ being come, an high priest of good things to come, Christ is now in place of all those oblations and sacrifices.

  Precepts:
  - **[Tobit 2:1](/bible/tobit/2#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/tobit/2#v1)</sup> Now when I was come home again, and my wife Anna was restored unto me, with my son Tobias, in the feast of Pentecost, which is the holy feast of the seven weeks, there was a good dinner prepared me, in the which I sat down to eat.

    Pentecost is the holy feast of the seven weeks, the seven sabbaths counted after the wave sheaf.
  - **[Colossians 2:16](/bible/colossians/2#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/colossians/2#v16)</sup> Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days:

    Let no man judge you in meat or in drink or in respect of an holyday; no man may condemn you for keeping the holy days without the sacrifices, now that Christ is come.
  - **[Hebrews 9:9-11](/bible/hebrews/9#v9)**
    > <sup>[9](/bible/hebrews/9#v9)</sup> Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;
    >
    > <sup>[10](/bible/hebrews/9#v10)</sup> Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.
    >
    > <sup>[11](/bible/hebrews/9#v11)</sup> But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building;

    The gifts and sacrifices were a figure for the time then present, carnal ordinances imposed until the time of reformation; Christ being come stands in place of them.

**[Leviticus 23:22](/bible/leviticus/23#v22)**

> <sup>[22](/bible/leviticus/23#v22)</sup> And when ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not make clean riddance of the corners of thy field when thou reapest, neither shalt thou gather any gleaning of thy harvest: thou shalt leave them unto the poor, and to the stranger: I am the Lord your God.

- When ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not make clean riddance of the corners of thy field, neither gather the gleaning of thy harvest: thou shalt leave them unto the poor and to the stranger.

**[Leviticus 23:23-25](/bible/leviticus/23#v23)**

> <sup>[23](/bible/leviticus/23#v23)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/leviticus/23#v24)</sup> Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall ye have a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/leviticus/23#v25)</sup> Ye shall do no servile work therein: but ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord.

- In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, is a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets. The new moon starts the new month, so the memorial of blowing of trumpets is a new moon; the seventh new moon is the special one, and that one is called the memorial of blowing of trumpets.
- The Most High made the moon to serve in her season for a declaration of times: from the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection. The moon is needed to calculate the feasts; the month is called after her name, because the new moon starts the new month, increasing wonderfully in her changing through the phases.
- But the moon has nothing to do with the seventh day Sabbath. The day starts at evening, for the evening and the morning were the first day; darkness was here first and has seniority. The moon was not even created on the first day of the week but on the fourth day, and the heavens and the earth were finished and the Most High still rested on the seventh day. The seven day rotation has run since the first day and nothing changes it; the Sabbath will always be Friday sundown to Saturday sundown.
- If the new moon falls on a seventh day Sabbath there is absolutely no cooking; the only day that permits cooking on the Sabbath is the Passover.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 43:6-8](/bible/sirach/43#v6)**
    > <sup>[6](/bible/sirach/43#v6)</sup> He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.
    >
    > <sup>[7](/bible/sirach/43#v7)</sup> From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/sirach/43#v8)</sup> The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her changing, being an instrument of the armies above, shining in the firmament of heaven;

    The moon serves for a declaration of times, and from the moon is the sign of feasts; the month is called after her name.
  - **[Genesis 1:14-19](/bible/genesis/1#v14)**
    > <sup>[14](/bible/genesis/1#v14)</sup> And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:
    >
    > <sup>[15](/bible/genesis/1#v15)</sup> And let them be for lights in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth: and it was so.
    >
    > <sup>[16](/bible/genesis/1#v16)</sup> And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.
    >
    > <sup>[17](/bible/genesis/1#v17)</sup> And God set them in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth,
    >
    > <sup>[18](/bible/genesis/1#v18)</sup> And to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness: and God saw that it was good.
    >
    > <sup>[19](/bible/genesis/1#v19)</sup> And the evening and the morning were the fourth day.

    The lights in the firmament were made for signs and for seasons, the lesser light to rule the night, on the fourth day; the moon came after the week was already counting.
  - **[Genesis 2:1-3](/bible/genesis/2#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/genesis/2#v1)</sup> Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/genesis/2#v2)</sup> And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/genesis/2#v3)</sup> And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made.

    The heavens and the earth were finished, and on the seventh day God ended his work and rested; the moon made on the fourth day did not dictate the seventh day Sabbath.

**[Leviticus 23:26-32](/bible/leviticus/23#v26)**

> <sup>[26](/bible/leviticus/23#v26)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/leviticus/23#v27)</sup> Also on the tenth day of this seventh month there shall be a day of atonement: it shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall afflict your souls, and offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/leviticus/23#v28)</sup> And ye shall do no work in that same day: for it is a day of atonement, to make an atonement for you before the Lord your God.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/leviticus/23#v29)</sup> For whatsoever soul it be that shall not be afflicted in that same day, he shall be cut off from among his people.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/leviticus/23#v30)</sup> And whatsoever soul it be that doeth any work in that same day, the same soul will I destroy from among his people.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/leviticus/23#v31)</sup> Ye shall do no manner of work: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations in all your dwellings.
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/leviticus/23#v32)</sup> It shall be unto you a sabbath of rest, and ye shall afflict your souls: in the ninth day of the month at even, from even unto even, shall ye celebrate your sabbath.

- On the tenth day of this seventh month, the same month as the blowing of trumpets, is the day of atonement, an holy convocation; ye shall afflict your souls, and do no manner of work in that same day, for whatsoever soul does any work that same day, that soul will the Most High destroy from among his people.
- To afflict your soul is to neither feed nor drink water nor taste anything, as Nineveh was commanded: no eating, no drinking, no tasting anything at all. That goes for gum, because you can taste gum, and even toothpaste; the last thing you do before the fast begins is brush your teeth before the sun goes down, and the first thing after it ends is brush them after the sun goes down. If you can taste it, keep it out of your mouth.
- From even unto even shall ye celebrate your sabbath, the ninth day of the month at even. Even unto even is how days are numbered, one complete day of twenty-four hours, not sunrise to sunrise, for the evening and the morning were the first day.

  Precepts:
  - **[Jonah 3:7](/bible/jonah/3#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/jonah/3#v7)</sup> And he caused it to be proclaimed and published through Nineveh by the decree of the king and his nobles, saying, Let neither man nor beast, herd nor flock, taste any thing: let them not feed, nor drink water:

    Let neither man nor beast taste any thing, nor feed, nor drink water; that is the affliction of the soul, tasting nothing at all.
  - **[Genesis 1:5](/bible/genesis/1#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/genesis/1#v5)</sup> And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And the evening and the morning were the first day.

    The evening and the morning were the first day; the day starts at evening, so the sabbath runs from even unto even.

**[Leviticus 23:33-44](/bible/leviticus/23#v33)**

> <sup>[33](/bible/leviticus/23#v33)</sup> And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/leviticus/23#v34)</sup> Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/leviticus/23#v35)</sup> On the first day shall be an holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein.
>
> <sup>[36](/bible/leviticus/23#v36)</sup> Seven days ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord: on the eighth day shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord: it is a solemn assembly; and ye shall do no servile work therein.
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/leviticus/23#v37)</sup> These are the feasts of the Lord, which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, to offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord, a burnt offering, and a meat offering, a sacrifice, and drink offerings, every thing upon his day:
>
> <sup>[38](/bible/leviticus/23#v38)</sup> Beside the sabbaths of the Lord, and beside your gifts, and beside all your vows, and beside all your freewill offerings, which ye give unto the Lord.
>
> <sup>[39](/bible/leviticus/23#v39)</sup> Also in the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when ye have gathered in the fruit of the land, ye shall keep a feast unto the Lord seven days: on the first day shall be a sabbath, and on the eighth day shall be a sabbath.
>
> <sup>[40](/bible/leviticus/23#v40)</sup> And ye shall take you on the first day the boughs of goodly trees, branches of palm trees, and the boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook; and ye shall rejoice before the Lord your God seven days.
>
> <sup>[41](/bible/leviticus/23#v41)</sup> And ye shall keep it a feast unto the Lord seven days in the year. It shall be a statute for ever in your generations: ye shall celebrate it in the seventh month.
>
> <sup>[42](/bible/leviticus/23#v42)</sup> Ye shall dwell in booths seven days; all that are Israelites born shall dwell in booths:
>
> <sup>[43](/bible/leviticus/23#v43)</sup> That your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.
>
> <sup>[44](/bible/leviticus/23#v44)</sup> And Moses declared unto the children of Israel the feasts of the Lord.

- The fifteenth day of the seventh month is the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto the Lord. The first day is an holy convocation with no servile work, and on the eighth day is an holy convocation, a solemn assembly.
- Ye shall take you on the first day the boughs of goodly trees, branches of palm trees, and the boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook, and rejoice before the Lord your God seven days. Those branches may be collected and put together in a vase in the home for the feast.
- Ye shall dwell in booths seven days, that your generations may know that the Most High made the children of Israel to dwell in booths when He brought them out of the land of Egypt, as when Israel was in the wilderness dwelling in tents.
- These laws are our culture, our history, and our heritage. The Passover is kept because the Most High delivered Israel out of the land of Egypt, not just some date we do for the kids; we do what this Bible says because the Most High commanded it, and all of His laws reflect our history.
